title: enMotion 10-Inch Automated vs. enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact: Sizing Touchless Dispensers by Room Type

excerpt: Choosing between the full-size Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-Inch Automated and the enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact depends on wall clearance, daily handwash traffic, and refill SKU standardization. See exact dimensional, roll footage, and janitorial restock comparisons for US office suites.
quickAnswer: The Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-Inch Automated dispenser is built for high-traffic multi-stall office restrooms ($15 to $30 per-visit janitorial scope), housing 10-inch-wide, 800-foot rolls (4,800 linear feet per 6-roll case), whereas the enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact uses a 35% smaller cabinet profile tailored for breakroom kitchenettes ($12 to $25/visit add-on scope) and tight single-occupant washrooms. Standardizing both properly keeps bundled consumable costs within the $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit national benchmark.

blocks.text: Why One Dispenser Footprint Rarely Fits Both Restrooms and Breakrooms

Facility managers outfitting a 5,000 to 25,000 sq ft office frequently attempt to install the exact same full-size 10-inch roll towel dispenser in every wet area—only to discover that a standard 14.8-inch-wide by 16.9-inch-tall cabinet simply will not fit between the upper millwork cabinets and the faucet gooseneck in the employee breakroom. Even in single-occupant executive or ADA unisex restrooms, narrow wing walls next to the mirror often leave less than 13 inches of horizontal mounting clearance.

Georgia-Pacific engineered the enMotion 10-Inch Automated and the enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact to solve this spatial split without forcing your janitorial team to learn two different internal electronics interfaces. However, because the two units take different roll widths (10-inch vs. 8-inch), deploying both across a building impacts your supply closet SKU count, case footage yield, and nightly restock cadence across the 4.33 weeks per month billing cycle.

blocks.title: Restroom vs. Breakroom Janitorial Pricing Benchmarks
blocks.text: In US commercial cleaning contracts, multi-fixture restroom sanitization adds $15 to $30 per restroom per visit, while Breakroom & Kitchenette Sanitation (countertops, sink, microwave interior/exterior, fridge exterior, and cabinet pulls) runs $12 to $25 per visit. Bundled paper and soap consumables add $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit. Right-sizing dispenser capacity to each zone prevents both unsightly countertop roll towels and mid-week dispenser run-outs.

blocks.text: When purchasing commercial paper refills such as the Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-Inch High-Capacity Paper Towel Rolls (6-roll case, 800 feet per roll = 4,800 total linear feet), you gain two distinct operational advantages over the 8-inch Impulse refill format. First, each 10-inch roll delivers 25% more paper width per linear inch dispensed, meaning occupants rarely trigger a second sensor cycle during a routine handwash. Second, the full-size 10-inch cabinet incorporates an internal stub-roll transfer tray: when the primary roll shrinks to roughly 2.5 inches in diameter, the evening custodian drops it into the lower stub caddy and loads a fresh 800-foot roll above it, achieving 100% paper consumption.

To achieve its compact 13.3-inch height and 8.6-inch depth, the enMotion Impulse 8-Inch dispenses from a single mandrel without a secondary stub-roll transfer shelf. In an office breakroom or single-user washroom where daily traffic is moderate, this is rarely an issue because a 700-foot roll lasts two to three weeks. However, in a high-traffic 4-stall corporate restroom cleaned 5x weekly (21.65 visits/month), lacking a stub-roll transfer mechanism forces night cleaners either to throw away the last 75 feet of paper on Friday night or risk an empty dispenser by Monday afternoon.

items: Under-Cabinet Breakroom Clearance: A typical US office kitchenette features an 18-inch vertical backsplash between the 36-inch counter deck and the 54-inch upper cabinets. The 13.3-inch-tall enMotion Impulse 8-Inch fits with nearly 5 inches of hand clearance below the chute, whereas the 16.9-inch-tall enMotion 10-Inch leaves only 1.1 inches—causing constant false sensor triggers.

Dual-Mode Sensor Flexibility: Both the 10-inch and Impulse 8-inch models include an internal toggle switch for 'On-Demand' (wave your hand to feed a towel) or 'Hanging Towel' mode (a fresh sheet automatically advances as soon as the previous sheet is torn off). Use 'On-Demand' in breakrooms to prevent accidental dispenses when employees reach for the sink faucet.

When 4-Inch ADA Protrusion Is Mandatory: Because both enMotion cabinets exceed 8.5 inches in depth, they must be positioned over a vanity counter footprint or inside an alcove to satisfy ADA Section 307.2. On exposed flat corridor walls without a counter below, specify a 4.0-inch-deep architectural cabinet like the Bobrick B-262 ClassicSeries 304 stainless steel folded dispenser.

Companion Level-Check Hardware: Pair your towel stations with the GOJO TFX Touch-Free Foam Soap Dispenser (featuring a top skylight window and 1,200 mL / 2,000-wash capacity) and the San Jamar Classic Oceans Twin 9-Inch Jumbo Tissue Dispenser (translucent housing) so night crews verify fill levels at a glance.

blocks.text: How Closet SKU Consolidation Affects Your Cleaning Quote

Every commercial janitorial closet in a 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft office ($0.09 to $0.15/sq ft cleaning benchmark) has limited shelving for chemical dilution jugs, HEPA vacuum bags, microfiber pads, and paper cases. If your facility has four multi-stall restrooms and two small breakroom sinks, stocking two different proprietary towel case SKUs (10-inch rolls for restrooms, 8-inch rolls for breakrooms) means storing at least two open 6-roll cartons simultaneously.

blocks.title: Custodial Loading Error Warning: 8-Inch Rolls in 10-Inch Cabinets
blocks.text: If you stock both 10-inch and 8-inch enMotion cases in the same janitor closet without clear shelf labels, new evening cleaners will inevitably attempt to force an 8-inch roll onto a 10-inch mandrel (or vice versa). Neither mandrel will engage the wrong roll width, leading to jammed doors or unstocked fixtures. Color-code shelf bins or standardize on a mid-sized cabinet like the Tork Elevation Matic H1 if you mandate a single building-wide towel SKU.

items.name: Measure Backsplash & Wing-Wall Clearances Across All Wet Zones
items.text: Record vertical height above countertops and horizontal distance from mirrors and door casings. Assign the enMotion 10-Inch to open multi-stall washroom walls with at least 24 inches of vertical clearance, and assign the Impulse 8-Inch to breakroom backsplashes with 16 to 18 inches of vertical clearance.

items.name: Configure Breakroom Units to Short Sheet & Wave-Only Mode
items.text: In office kitchenettes, employees frequently grab paper towels to wipe a coffee drip or dry a single mug. Set the Impulse 8-Inch internal switch to the shortest sheet length and Wave-On-Demand mode to cut breakroom paper waste by up to 35%.

items.name: Verify Floor Care Multipliers Around Wet Dispenser Zones
items.text: Breakrooms often feature VCT/LVT vinyl (1.04x flooring cost multiplier) or polished concrete (0.95x multiplier), while restrooms use ceramic tile and grout (1.12x multiplier). Position towel dispensers within arm's reach of the sink basin so wet hands never drip across floor transitions on the way to the trash can.

items.name: Benchmark Consumable Add-On Quotes Against Case Consumption
items.text: At 4,800 linear feet per 6-roll case (enMotion 10-inch), a case delivers roughly 5,230 hand dries at an 11-inch setting. Compare your actual monthly case usage against your janitorial vendor's $0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit consumables add-on to verify fair contract pricing.

faqs.q: Are Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-inch paper towel rolls compatible with the enMotion Impulse 8-inch dispenser?
faqs.a: No. The enMotion 10-Inch Automated dispenser requires 10-inch-wide rolls (such as the 89460 series 800-ft rolls), whereas the enMotion Impulse 8-Inch Compact requires 8-inch-wide rolls (such as the 89410/89420 series 700-ft rolls). The internal roll holders and feed rollers are fixed to their respective 10-inch and 8-inch widths.

faqs.q: What is the minimum vertical clearance needed to mount an enMotion dispenser above a breakroom countertop?
faqs.a: You need at least 6 to 8 inches of clear space between the bottom dispensing slot and the countertop or faucet arc so the downward-facing infrared sensor does not reflect off the counter surface. That means the 13.3-inch-tall Impulse 8-Inch needs roughly 19 to 21 inches of total vertical height, while the 16.9-inch-tall enMotion 10-Inch requires 23 to 25 inches—which is why the 10-inch model rarely fits beneath standard 18-inch breakroom upper cabinets.

faqs.q: When should an office use a stainless steel folded dispenser like the Bobrick B-262 instead of an enMotion roll unit?
faqs.a: Use a surface-mounted 304 stainless steel folded cabinet like the Bobrick B-262 (which projects exactly 4.0 inches from the wall) whenever the dispenser must be mounted on an open pedestrian circulation wall with no counter beneath it. Because automated roll cabinets project 8.6 to 9.75 inches, mounting them on an unprotected open corridor or restroom wall violates the ADA Section 307.2 4-inch maximum protrusion limit unless recessed into the studs.

faqs.q: How does adding Breakroom & Kitchenette Sanitation affect our monthly janitorial invoice?
faqs.a: In standard US commercial janitorial contracts, Breakroom & Kitchenette Sanitation is priced at $12 to $25 per visit (covering sink scrubbing, countertop disinfection, microwave interior/exterior wiping, fridge handles, and towel/soap restocking). Across a 3x-weekly schedule (13.0 visits/month at 4.33 weeks/month), a dedicated breakroom scope adds $156 to $325 per month; across a 5x-weekly schedule (21.65 visits/month), it adds $260 to $541 per month.
